works_at.note: NOT LINKED, DELIBERATELY. He plastered data/structures/chicago_democrat_office in November 1833 - a single documented job, twenty months before the scene date - and a works_at pointing there would read as employment. A jobbing plasterer in July 1835 was somewhere else.

present_on_scene_date.note: PRESENCE ON THE SCENE DATE IS AN ASSUMPTION OF CONTINUITY AND NOT A STATEMENT. Nothing reached follows this household past 1833. It is graded uncertain rather than present because the town's population roughly quadrupled between the roster and the scene date and a great many of the men on it were, in Andreas's own phrase, 'adventurers, comprising moneyed speculators and prospectors, as yet undecided whether to stay at Chicago or go on'.

persons.name: Ashbel Steele

occupation.note: 'Ashbel Steele, plastered Calhoun's printing office in November, 1833' - the trade is stated as an act rather than as a title, which is how this roster names several of its artisans.

persons.note: Andreas vol. 1, printed p. 132 (scan p. 281), 'an imperfect list of the denizens of the town in the fall of 1833, not before named'. It gives a name, a trade and usually an arrival year, and it is a retrospective of 1884: a YEAR off it is documented, a MONTH is not, and it says nothing whatever about 1835.

resident_research.evidence_for: Cook County histories place Ashbel Steele in the early Chicago/Cook County civic record and identify him as county coroner in the 1835 period. This supports continued local presence while stopping short of assigning an unsourced town dwelling.

research_note: THE ONLY PLASTERER IN THE DATASET, AND THE ONLY MAN IN IT DOCUMENTED BY A SINGLE JOB. What makes him worth a record is what the job proves about a building: the town's ordinances of 7 November 1833 legislate for 'wooden buildings with wooden and lath-and-plaster partitions', and this is a named man doing exactly that work in the same month, in a building this dataset models. THE LINK IS NOT MADE IN works_at because plastering a room once is not working somewhere; it is recorded here.
